correctness.rationale: The source fold equation gives an exact two-root formula. Substitution into the source definition of the fold activity reduces it to a one-variable analytic function whose first derivative vanishes and whose second and third derivatives at coalescence are explicit. Taylor expansion yields the positive three-halves branch difference, and the analytic map from the source parameter b to temperature transfers it with the stated amplitude. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source itself uses the two fold curves as the exact boundary of its three-positive-solution region and explicitly identifies their meeting point as a cusp. Quantifying the collapse of that region by a universal exponent and an exact all-parameter amplitude gives a natural structural invariant of the phase diagram and sharpens the source endpoint result, rather than adding a routine special-case computation.
